flawed_step: The step claiming planarity forces at least one relevant Kempe chain to be disconnected. With neighbours v1..v5 coloured 1,2,1,3,4, a single interchange fails for pairs {1,2},{1,3},{1,4} if the chain through the unique 2-, 3- or 4-coloured neighbour reaches v1 or v3. It fails for pairs {2,3},{2,4},{3,4} if v2, v4, v5 are pairwise chain-linked. Planarity does not rule out all of these at once (Kempe's degree-5 error).
counterexample: G has vertices v, v1..v5. Edges: v to each vi; the cycle v1v2, v2v3, v3v4, v4v5, v5v1; chords v2v4 and v2v5. It is planar: the wheel with both chords drawn outside the pentagon, 12 = 3*6-6 edges. c on G-v: v1=1, v2=2, v3=1, v4=3, v5=4; proper, and all 4 colours are on N(v). Kempe components and neighbour colours (v1..v5) after swapping: {1,2}: {v1,v2,v3} -> 2,1,2,3,4. {1,3}: {v1} -> 3,2,1,3,4; {v3,v4} -> 1,2,3,1,4. {1,4}: {v1,v5} -> 4,2,1,3,1; {v3} -> 1,2,4,3,4. {2,3}: {v2,v4} -> 1,3,1,2,4. {2,4}: {v2,v5} -> 1,4,1,3,2. {3,4}: {v4,v5} -> 1,2,1,4,3. All 9 single interchanges leave 4 colours on N(v).
assessment_summary: The statement is the Kempe fallacy for degree 5. In a 6-vertex planar triangulation (a 5-wheel plus chords v2v4 and v2v5), the colouring 1,2,1,3,4 on the neighbours has the chains {2,3}, {2,4} and {3,4} pairwise linking the singly coloured neighbours. Each of those neighbours is also chain-linked to a colour-1 neighbour. Checking every Kempe component shows no single interchange removes a colour from N(v).
